title: Why Smoke Alarms Chirp at 3 A.M.
topic: Low-battery chirp is triggered when cool night air drops battery voltage; replace alarms after 10 years

beats.narration: That 3 a.m. chirp means your smoke alarm is dying.
beats.caption: YOUR ALARM IS DYING
beats.direction: Serious, urgent, a low warning in the dark. Lean on 'dying'.

beats.narration: And it's not bad luck it happens at night.
beats.caption: NOT BAD LUCK

beats.narration: That chirp is a low-battery warning.
beats.caption: LOW BATTERY

beats.narration: Homes are usually coolest between two and six a.m.
beats.caption: COOLEST AT 2–6 AM

beats.narration: The temperature drops, and the battery's voltage dips.
beats.caption: VOLTAGE DIPS

beats.narration: So the alarm thinks it's out of power. Chirp.
beats.caption: CHIRP.
beats.direction: Deadpan, land the 'Chirp' as a punchline.

beats.narration: That's why it picks the worst possible hour.
beats.caption: THE WORST HOUR

beats.narration: Swap the battery, and the chirping should stop.
beats.caption: SWAP THE BATTERY

beats.narration: Still chirping with a fresh one?
beats.caption: STILL CHIRPING?

beats.narration: Check the date on the back. After about ten years, replace the whole alarm.
beats.caption: 10 YEARS = REPLACE

beats.narration: Three in five home fire deaths happen with no working alarm.
beats.caption: 3 IN 5

beats.narration: Save this for the next time it chirps at three a.m.
beats.caption: SAVE THIS FOR 3 AM
beats.direction: Friendly, warm, a little knowing smile.
